messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a perf spike for small-batch inference on /v1/generate after the kernel-selector update. KV hit-rate for that route dropped ~12% in the 01:00-02:00 UTC window. Investigating, pinging @maria and @ryan.

maria: thanks. do you have a sample request id or trace? will pull per-request breakdowns.

alex: example request_id=req_2026_9a3b, trace_id=tr_9a3b. From token-level histogram: tail tokens show a +6ms median increase in "kv_lookup" bucket and a larger spread in "kernel_select" time.

ryan: saw deploy-bot note earlier: deploy-bot: kernel-selector v2 rolled at 1849100000 — fallback rules changed to prefer fused-kernel for seq_len<=64. Could be a mismatch with batching heuristics.

maria: grabbing console tiles now. Per-route KPI (from grafana):
```
route: /v1/generate
p50_token_latency: 2.8ms -> 3.6ms
p95_token_latency: 9.2ms -> 11.7ms
kv_hit_rate: 78% -> 66%
avg_effective_batch_size: 4.7 -> 3.1
```

alex: that average batch size drop is suspicious. maybe runtime changed batching window or reuse of KV cache keys is broken for the fused-kernel path.

ryan: I pulled a flame on the trace: https://traces.internal/trace/tr_9a3b — shows a 14ms pause between token generation steps where the kernel selection RPC happens. The selection RPC is async now and waits for batch-completion signal. For single-stream small batches that adds overhead.

ops-oncall: noted the alert. rolling back to kernel-selector v1 for the dedicated pool would be quick if we confirm root cause. Any quick config toggle we can test?

maria: we can force kernel selection to prefer legacy-kernel for routes with avg_batch_size < 5 via a routing policy. Query for candidate requests: `sum by(route) (rate(inference_requests[5m]) / sum by(route) (in_flight_batch_size))` — will give effective batch size estimate.

alex: also adding trace->metric link in dashboard: when you click a per-request row show `trace_id` column that links to trace service. Eg `https://traces.internal/trace/{{trace_id}}`. That helped me confirm the selection RPC latency.

ryan: proposal: add token-level breakdown column to per-request view: {total_token_ms, kernel_select_ms, kv_lookup_ms, device_ms, queue_ms}. This is already in runtime span but not surfaced in UI. I can add the schema change to the telemetry exporter.

maria: +1. minimal change first: expose kv_hit boolean and kernel_variant label in metrics so we can slice KPIs by kernel_variant. Query example: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{kernel_variant!=""}[5m])) by (le, route, kernel_variant))`

alex: for immediate mitigation, ops-oncall can flip routing policy to prefer legacy-kernel for /v1/generate until ryans change is live. Then we'll run a canary with v2 and the updated telemetry.

ops-oncall: I'm on it, flipping policy now for dedicated pool. Also creating an incident ticket with the trace and metric links.

ryan: I'll push telemetry change and a small runtime flag to short-circuit async selection for batches < 6 so we avoid the extra RPC. Will post PR link when ready.

maria: once PR is up, I'll add dashboard tiles: per-route kv_hit_rate, kernel_variant split, and per-request token-level table with trace links. That should make future correlation immediate.

alex: thanks team. leaving a note: owners should also check quantization-induced key normalization; earlier bug turned some cache keys into floats which reduced hits. Might be unrelated but worth a quick sanity check.

ryan: noted. will add a small health-check that validates key formats and emits a metric `kv_key_format_errors`.

alex: great. closing loop: ops-oncall — confirm when rollback complete and post incident ticket id here.

ops-oncall: rollback done at 1849123500, incident: INC-2026-314. Will monitor for 30m. :eyes:
